name: UW Mock Trial
description: A small competitive team, founded in 2007, that simulates full criminal and civil trials; members play attorneys and witnesses and travel nationally to tournaments.

commitment.hours_per_week: ~7 hrs/wk (Tue/Thu 2 hrs + Sat 3 hrs; more before tournaments)

dues: No dues listed (confirm with officers); members pay own airfare and food for travel, team covers lodging
meeting_schedule: Practices Tue & Thu 6-8pm and Sat 10am-1pm; Mon-Thu 6-8pm the week before a tournament
fit_reason: Aspiring lawyers and performers who want intense, travel-heavy courtroom competition.

application.deadline: Auditions Oct 8, 10 and 11, 2026 (2026-27 season; next cycle unknown)
steps: Attend an info session (required to get an audition slot)
Prepare a memorized ~2.5-min persuasive speech on a topic of your choice
Prepare a ~2.5-min monologue from the team's list
Audition, including a short Q&A

interest_areas: Research/competitive teams (robotics, case competitions, Model UN)

name: Washington iGEM
description: An undergraduate-run synthetic biology research team founded in 2008 that competes in the international iGEM competition, with wet lab, dry lab, human practices, and wiki/design subteams.

commitment.hours_per_week: ~5-10 hrs/wk in the school year; ~10-20 in summer

fit_reason: Students of any major wanting a year-long, hands-on research project with an international competition.

application.deadline: Applications open in December; interviews in January (exact dates unknown)
steps: Submit online application with resume and short statement of interest
Casual interview if selected (January)
Join a subteam and onboard (February)

interest_areas: Research/competitive teams (robotics, case competitions, Model UN)

name: Quizbowl at the University of Washington
description: An intercollegiate quizbowl team and student club whose practices read academic question packets, then pop culture questions and socializing; some members compete nationally, and UW teams have placed at ICT.
meeting_schedule: Mondays and Thursdays at 7:00 PM (Fall Quarter, from Thu Oct 1); location TBA on site
fit_reason: Trivia lovers who want low-pressure practices with the option to travel to tournaments.

steps: Show up to any practice (no experience needed)
Join the Discord for announcements and online practices

interest_areas: Research/competitive teams (robotics, case competitions, Model UN)

name: Reformed University Fellowship (RUF UW)
description: A campus ministry of "a diverse group of students seeking to know, love, and serve Jesus together in community"; it says it is not just for Christians and is open to anyone exploring faith.
meeting_schedule: Large Group Wednesdays 8 PM in Johnson Hall (JHN) 102; First-Year Fellowship Mondays 7 PM in the HUB
fit_reason: Students wanting weekly Christian worship and community, including those just exploring faith.

steps: Show up to Wednesday Large Group or Monday First-Year Fellowship

name: Hillel UW: Center for Jewish Life on Campus
description: A campus Jewish community serving Jewish students from a broad range of backgrounds with Shabbat and holiday observances, learning, cultural, social, social justice and Israel programs; its Welcome Back Shabbat said everyone is welcome regardless of background or observance.
meeting_schedule: Weekly Torah Learning with Rabbi Lauren (listed Tue Oct 20); Friday Shabbat dinners (e.g., Oct 2 song circle 5:15 PM, dinner 6:30 PM) at 4745 17th Ave NE
fit_reason: Jewish students, of any level of observance, looking for Shabbat, learning and community.

steps: Check the calendar at hilleluw.org and RSVP to an event

name: Chabad Jewish Student Group (Chabad UW)
description: Chabad UW helps Jewish students connect with community and grow their Jewish knowledge, with a free homemade four-course Friday Shabbat dinner open to all Jewish Huskies, a weekly JewDub Tent on Red Square, and classes.
dues: No dues listed (confirm with officers); Shabbat dinner is free
meeting_schedule: Free Shabbat dinner Friday nights; JewDub Tent weekly on Red Square (time not listed); weekly classes
fit_reason: Jewish students who want free Shabbat dinners, holiday celebrations and Jewish learning.

steps: Follow @chabaduw for the calendar
Come to Friday Shabbat dinner

name: Catholic Newman Center at UW
description: The Prince of Peace Catholic Newman Center, run by the Dominicans, serves UW students with daily Mass, confession, adoration, small groups, retreats and a monthly Diving Deeper talk series.
dues: No dues listed (confirm with officers); fall retreat $75 with scholarships
meeting_schedule: Sunday Mass 10am, 5pm, 7pm, 9pm; Wednesday 9pm; Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri 12:35pm; Diving Deeper third Thursdays 7pm; at 4502 20th Ave NE
fit_reason: Catholic students wanting Mass near campus plus retreats, service and small groups.

steps: Attend Mass or a student event
Fill out the Small Group Interest Form

name: The Daily
description: The University of Washington's 100% student-run news organization, established in 1891, publishing online and in print. Staff from all majors work as writers, photographers, videographers, designers, copy editors, illustrators and audio journalists.

commitment.hours_per_week: ~4 hrs/wk (copy editors: two 2-hr shifts); up to 15 for lead sports writers

dues: No dues listed; staff are paid per assignment
meeting_schedule: New writers and photographers take a quarter-long development course with weekly classes (day/time couldn't confirm)
fit_reason: Aspiring journalists, photographers and designers who want paid, published portfolio work.

application.deadline: Autumn 2026 deadlines (Sept 16 to Oct 2) have passed; most roles reopen at the end of the quarter
steps: Check open positions on the Join Us page
Apply by the posted deadline (writers apply to the Daily 101 program)
Complete the quarter-long development course

name: Rainy Dawg Radio
description: UW Seattle's only student-run radio station, founded in the early 2000s and broadcasting from HUB 131N. More than 50 volunteer DJs host weekly one-hour live shows, and the Blawg publishes music writing.

commitment.hours_per_week: ~1 hr/wk on air (DJs); 1-hr weekly Blawg meeting

meeting_schedule: Blawg meetings Fridays 2-3pm in the studio (HUB 131N); DJs host a weekly 1-hour show
fit_reason: Music lovers who want their own weekly radio show or to write music journalism.

application.deadline: DJ applications open Oct 26, 2026 and close Nov 9, 2026 (once a year)
steps: Apply on rainydawg.org during the Fall DJ window
Or just come to a Friday Blawg meeting with an article pitch

name: Bricolage Literary & Visual Arts Journal
description: UW's undergraduate literary and visual arts journal, publishing prose, poetry and visual art in an annual issue since 1983, plus a zine. It is run by undergraduate volunteer staff who handle editing, production and outreach.

commitment.hours_per_week: 1-2 hrs/wk in fall, 4-5 in winter (editor roles)

meeting_schedule: Editorial team meets weekly; all-staff meeting quarterly
fit_reason: Writers and artists who want hands-on literary editing and publishing experience.

application.deadline: Issue 45 staff applications are closed; submissions and volunteer reviewing also available
steps: Submit work or volunteer to review submissions
Apply for a staff role when applications open (UW Seattle undergrads)
Email brico@uw.edu with questions

name: Grey Matters Journal
description: A UW student-run nonprofit that makes neuroscience accessible, publishing a quarterly undergraduate neuroscience journal and running public events and K-12 outreach. Roles span writing, editing, design, illustration, translation, podcasting and operations.
meeting_schedule: Production team holds weekly writing sessions; quarterly welcome meetings and Journal Club are open to all
fit_reason: Science-curious students of any major who want to write, edit or design for publication.

application.deadline: unknown (some Production and Operations roles listed as open)
steps: Pick a position on the Applications page
Submit a separate application per role (UW NetID sign-in required)

name: Husky Tetris Club
description: A UW club bringing together Tetris players of all skill levels, home to UW's Collegiate Tetris League semifinalist team. Hangouts feature score battles and head-to-head Classic and Modern Tetris.
fit_reason: Block-stackers of any level who want casual play or a shot at collegiate Tetris competition.

steps: Join the club Discord
Drop in to a Tuesday meeting in SAV 132

name: Mahjong Society at UW
description: A beginner-friendly community of students who learn and play mahjong variants including Riichi, Hong Kong and Taiwanese; no gambling. Runs weekly general meetings, monthly workshops and tournaments.
meeting_schedule: Official general meetings Tuesdays 5-7 PM at HUB Games; monthly workshops (Riichi Workshop Oct 28, 2026, 5-7 PM, Spratlen Hall 311)
fit_reason: Anyone curious about mahjong, from total beginners to experienced Riichi players.

steps: Join the Discord for updates and spontaneous games
Show up Tuesday 5-7 PM at HUB Games
RSVP for workshops via the Linktree forms

name: UW Costume Club
description: A creative club for sewing, mending and costume-making, with officers teaching machine and hand sewing basics. Weekly drop-in sessions in Hutchinson Hall.
dues: No dues listed; Discord is free to join (confirm with officers)
meeting_schedule: Thursdays 6-10 PM, Hutchinson Hall 135 (drop-in; building locks at 5 PM, ask officers on Discord to be let in)
fit_reason: Crafters and cosplayers wanting hands-on sewing help and a creative community, no experience needed.

steps: Join the Discord
Drop in Thursday 6-10 PM at Hutchinson 135

name: Anime Discovery Project
description: UW's original anime RSO (since 1991), holding weekly showings of lesser-known anime chosen each quarter, with a movie the week before finals. Welcomes all UW-affiliated anime lovers.
meeting_schedule: Weekly anime showings during the quarter (day/time posted on Discord)
fit_reason: Anime fans who want to discover new shows and watch together each week.

steps: Join the ADP Discord for showing times
Attend a weekly showing

name: UW Chess Club
description: A campus chess club open to all skill levels, with weekly puzzles, 5-minute blitz tournaments, casual games and Bughouse. Co-hosts the Husky Open tournament with the Washington Chess Federation.
dues: No dues listed for weekly meetings; Husky Open entry is $20-25 for UW students
fit_reason: Chess players of any rating wanting relaxed weekly games plus the occasional rated tournament.

steps: Join the mailing list on the club site
Drop in Tuesday 3:30-5 PM in HUB 337

name: UW Esports
description: UW's official competitive gaming program, with teams in Valorant, League of Legends, Super Smash Bros. Ultimate and Rocket League that play weekly; it is joining the Power Esports Conference. Students can also volunteer in shoutcasting, production and outreach.
dues: No dues listed for teams (confirm with officers); HUB Games PC time is $3.50/hr for students
meeting_schedule: Teams play weekly; official matches Mondays from 4:30 PM and Wednesdays 4:30-9 PM in the HUB Esports Lounge
fit_reason: Serious competitive gamers, plus aspiring casters and broadcast techs.

steps: Join the UW Esports Discord
Fill out the tryout form in #Recruitment (or the volunteer form)
